sections.content: You know *el que fuera presidente*, *la ciudad donde naciera* and *como dijera el cronista* from B2 Unit 15: in formal journalism, plaques and historical essays, the *-ra* form can carry a factual past-indicative value equivalent to *había* + participle or the preterite. At C1, the challenge is reading both uses of *-ra* side by side in the same text: factual indicative *-ra* (where *-se* is excluded) versus true subjunctive *-ra* after *si*, *aunque* or an unidentified antecedent (you know *que tenga* from B2 Unit 13), where *-se* is interchangeable.

sections.title: Two uses of -ra in historical prose
rows: El recinto que albergara la hemeroteca cerró en 1998.
Indicative *-ra* (= *había albergado / albergó*): known factual building; *-se* is not used.
Como señalara la semblanza oficial, la placa se colocó en el centenario.
Indicative *-ra* (= *señaló / había señalado*): factual citation after *como*.
Buscaban un testigo que recordara la inscripción original.
Aunque el obituario omitiera aquel episodio, las cartas lo confirman.
True subjunctive *-ra* (= *omitiese*): concessive clause; non-factual or backgrounded.

items.spanish: En la placa figura el nombre del arquitecto que diseñara el recinto hace un siglo.
items.english: On the plaque appears the name of the architect who designed the grounds a century ago.

items.spanish: La efeméride recuerda la escuela donde enseñara la maestra antes de trasladarse a la capital.
items.english: The anniversary commemorates the school where the teacher had taught before moving to the capital.

items.spanish: El comité buscaba una fotografía que mostrara la plaza antes de la reforma.
items.english: The committee was looking for a photograph that showed the square before the renovation.

items.spanish: Como recordara el obituario publicado este mes, su labor impulsó el archivo municipal.
items.english: As the obituary published this month recalled, her work drove the municipal archive forward.

sections.content: Only the *-ra* form carries this indicative past value; *-se* cannot replace it in *el edificio que albergara el archivo*. In your own speech and everyday writing, the standard indicative (*había albergado* or *albergó*) is always natural; treat indicative *-ra* as a formal reading register and test whether the clause states a verified fact or an open condition.
